A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iS-QN research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original online and offline Atari experiments, head-count and normalization ablations, and gradient and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original Atari results and adds original continuous-control, Wordle, target-stability, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The shared-feature architecture, frozen first head, Equation 1, and DQN pseudocode remain intact. New adaptations include discounting successive SAC losses by 0.25, corresponding aggregation of critic predictions in the policy loss, and averaging ILQL advantage weights across heads (Section 5.3 and Appendix C).

E1.justification: Beyond the retained online and offline Atari coverage, v2 evaluates seven DMC Hard continuous-control tasks and offline Wordle using the Wordle Twitter dataset. These introduce continuous actions and language-based, multi-turn decision making.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator families expand from DQN/CQL to target-based and target-free SAC with SimbaV2, and target-based and target-free ILQL (Figures 6–7). The Atari comparator sets, including ES-CQL, are retained. Figure 19 additionally compares TB-SAC with and without BatchNorm.

E3.justification: New protocols include distributional SAC with soft target updates, 500,000 training steps and action repeat 2, and GPT-2-small ILQL with 800,000 gradient steps (Tables 2–3). SAC uses BatchNorm for TF-SAC and iS-SAC but excludes it from TB-SAC. v2 also specifies cumulative, periodically reset, TF-normalized target-churn measurement. Existing Atari settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds target-churn analysis to test target stability (Figure 8), DMC representation-rank and dormant-neuron analyses plus a BatchNorm control (Figure 19), and runtime/FLOP comparisons (Appendix B). Earlier head-count, normalization, gradient-similarity, and ensemble analyses remain; the offline effective-rank analysis is relocated.

E5.justification: v2 specifies ten seeds per DMC task and five for Wordle. Five Atari seeds, IQM aggregation, and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals are retained. This adds experiment-specific run information without establishing increased runs for existing Atari experiments.

E6.justification: Headline Atari AUC findings remain, including the 6% CNN-LayerNorm advantage and CQL gap reduction from 26% to 6%, although some plotted estimates, including cosine similarities, change. New results report DMC gap recovery with iS-SAC K=1 and 49% fewer total model parameters, and over 5% higher normalized Wordle AUC with iS-ILQL K=9 and 33% fewer parameters. Target-churn and runtime/FLOP results are also added.

T1.justification: Section 5.5 introduces target churn as the absolute difference between regression targets before and after a batch update, with cumulative reset and normalization rules. This adds a defined mathematical quantity. Existing Bellman relations and Equation 1 remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains sharing online features with frozen linear heads and learning successive Bellman updates to improve target-free sample efficiency while retaining a low Q-network memory footprint. The broader evaluations support this retained claim rather than redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a policy-churn analogy and interprets target-churn measurements as evidence of greater target stability. Its new limitations discussion addresses setting-dependent head counts, replay-buffer and optimizer memory, unchanged inference memory, and generally unchanged computation. Continuous control moves beyond v1's future-work status; pruning and quantization become proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D add DMC and Wordle setup and hyperparameter details, timing hardware and tasks, normalization placement and batching, IMPALA layer sizes, and the previously unspecified Atari CQL weight of 0.1. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments. The reproducibility statement additionally says supplementary code contains versioned dependencies; public release remains conditional on acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting SAC, ILQL, Wordle, DMC, policy churn, and critic/actor sizing. It also refines its positioning against i-QN: v1 describes storing 2K networks, whereas v2 acknowledges shared online representations while identifying retained target copies as the memory burden. The main target-free literature survey remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, the title shortened, and the author list updated. Existing explanations receive local refinements, while algorithmic appendix notes are regrouped and reproducibility and language-model-use statements are added. Most original prose and the main narrative sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds continuous-control, Wordle, computational-cost, and DMC diagnostic figures plus two hyperparameter tables. It recomposes the mechanism figure, relocates offline effective rank, reorganizes the CQL learning-curve grid, and adds memory annotations. Formatting and captions change throughout; Figure 15 introduces a TB-DQN caption label inconsistent with its retained TF-DQN plot.

improvement.justification: v1's evidence was restricted to Atari, left continuous control for future work, and asserted comparable training time without reporting timing measurements. v2 adds distinct continuous-control and language evaluations, directly measures target stability, and benchmarks runtime and FLOPs. These address substantive gaps in applicability and support for the resource-efficiency argument. Expanded implementation details and explicit memory/computation limitations further improve assessability. Minor new caption and cross-reference errors do not outweigh these gains.
